name: Carmine (cochineal)
note: Crushed cochineal insects, used as a red colourant. Not vegan.

name: Lanolin
note: Grease from sheep's wool. Not vegan.

name: Gelatin
note: Made by boiling animal bones, skin and connective tissue. Not vegan.

name: Collagen
note: Usually derived from animal skin, bone or connective tissue, unless labelled 'vegan collagen' or 'plant collagen'. Not vegan.

name: Keratin
note: Usually derived from animal hair, horns or hooves, unless labelled 'vegetable keratin'. Not vegan.

name: Elastin
note: A protein extracted from animal connective tissue. Not vegan.

name: Shellac
note: A resin secreted by the lac bug. Not vegan.

name: Beeswax
note: Made by honeybees. Not vegan.

name: Honey
note: Made by honeybees. Not vegan.

name: Royal jelly
note: A bee secretion fed to larvae. Not vegan.

name: Propolis
note: A resin bees make from plant sap, mixed with beeswax. Not vegan.

name: Tallow
note: Rendered animal fat, often from cattle or sheep. Not vegan.

name: Casein
note: A milk protein. Not vegan.

name: Whey
note: A milk by-product. Not vegan.

name: Lactose
note: Milk sugar. Not vegan.

name: Albumin
note: Usually derived from egg white or animal blood serum. Not vegan.

name: Guanine (pearl essence)
note: A shimmer ingredient made from fish scales. Not vegan.

name: Ambergris
note: A substance from sperm whale digestive tracts, used in some perfumes. Not vegan.

name: Musk
note: Traditionally taken from musk deer glands. Modern fragrances usually use a synthetic substitute, but it isn't always specified. Not vegan unless labelled synthetic.

name: Civet
note: A secretion from civet cats, used in some perfumes. Not vegan.

name: Silk
note: Made by silkworms, usually boiled alive in production. Not vegan.

name: Squalene
note: Historically shark liver oil. Increasingly plant-derived (olives, sugarcane) but the source isn't always stated, and it's a different substance from the usually-plant-derived 'squalane'. Worth checking with the brand.

name: Glycerin
note: Can come from animal fat, plant oils, or be synthetic. Most commercial glycerin today is plant-derived, but it isn't guaranteed from the ingredient name alone.

name: Stearic acid
note: Can be derived from animal fat or plant oils (like palm or coconut). Usually plant-derived commercially, but not guaranteed from the name alone.

name: Lecithin
note: Usually derived from soy or sunflower, but can occasionally be egg-derived. Worth checking if it doesn't say 'soy lecithin' or 'sunflower lecithin'.

name: Vitamin D3
note: Often derived from lanolin (sheep's wool grease). Vitamin D2 (ergocalciferol) is plant-derived and vegan; D3 usually isn't unless specified as lichen-derived.

name: Oleic acid
note: Can be derived from animal fat or plant oils. Usually plant-derived commercially, but not guaranteed from the name alone.

name: Allantoin
note: Can be synthesised, or derived from comfrey root or animal urine. Almost always synthetic commercially, but not guaranteed from the name alone.
